rows.notes: Installed 1 GWh/yr (company/press basis, Nation Thailand 2024-04-09 quoting 'gigawatt per hour', read as GWh/yr; EA 2021 release also says 'initial capacity of 1 GWh per year'). Nameplate 4 GWh = EA's dated target 'by the end of 2025' (ref_year 2025); the 2021 release also says phase 1 can expand to 4 GWh/yr. EA's 50 GWh/yr ambition is an undated company aspiration (D-015), excluded. Installed figure is >18 months old at 2026-11-20 so confidence capped 0.5. No 2025-26 news found on actual output or on whether the 4 GWh was reached. start_year (v1 2021) not nulled for lack of truth but for lack of a quotable year: Nation 2021-12-13 grand-opening release (S8) is dated Dec 2021; no explicit production-start sentence quoted. v1 chemistry 'lithium-ion' not in vocabulary -> null; v1 end_market mixed not re-confirmed -> null; v1 capacity_by_year_json {2021:1} not sourced as ramp -> null.

APB (Echizen, Fukui) received a bankruptcy commencement order from Fukui District Court on 2025-04-23 (TSR, S9); on 2025-06 a basic agreement to start talks on business transfer to Critical Path (founder Horie's new company) was reported (S10); no later news found that the transfer closed or the plant restarted. Per D-018: bankrupt/idle built plant -> project_state paused, installed null. Plant was newly built in 2021 'for mass production' but TSR (2025-03-18, S11) says all-resin battery mass production 'had no prospect' (量産化 目途が立っていない) -> it never reached commercial scale; status kept 'operational' only as pilot/verification-scale production reached 2021 (v1) - low confidence, status could arguably be under_construction/null; lead may decide. v1 nameplate 3.0 GWh and ramp JSON {2021:0.2} could not be sourced -> null. v1 start_year 2021 not quotable with production start -> null. Chemistry set to 'other': all-polymer (resin-coated bipolar electrode) lithium-ion; the LFP cathode in v1 is not supported by any page I fetched, so not set to LFP. Format/end_market left as v1 (pouch/ESS) - not re-verified. Coordinates unchanged (Echizen).

v1 nameplate 20 GWh / ref 2030 / confidence 0.7 is WRONG for this row: 20 GWh is the separate new BEV cell plant (Honda/GS Yuasa/Blue Energy, METI-certified, in Shiga) already carried as row blue-energy-co-ltd-honda-gs-yuasa-new-battery-plant-... (T013). This row = the existing HEV lithium-ion cell plant at 1-37 Osadano-cho, Fukuchiyama, Kyoto; mass production since Feb 2011 (company outline S12), a second plant added on the same GS Yuasa Osadano property in Oct 2021 (same source). No GWh figure published: GS Yuasa's 2021-04-12 release gives GS Yuasa-wide HEV output 'Approx. 20 million cells' per year growing to ~50 million cells planned FY2023 (S13; company-wide, in cells not GWh) -> nameplate null. v1 chemistry/format not confirmed (null). Honda (49%) / GS Yuasa (51%) JV unchanged. Coordinates unchanged.

Durapower's own release places its cell manufacturing in Suzhou, China (new 2.0 GWh/yr factory broke ground 2024-03-15); Singapore is the headquarters ('Headquartered in Singapore'). No Singapore cell plant exists in any source found. Row was an HQ mis-attribution (v1 already had is_cell_manufacturer false). The Suzhou plants are NOT in the database (see Discoveries).

Energy Innovation Group, Ltd. (registered office #70, 3-ro, 4-sandan, Jiksan-eup, Seobuk-gu, Cheonan-si; website eigbattery.com) was declared bankrupt by the Daejeon District Court (2019 Hahap 7074); a foreign representative filed a Chapter 15 petition in N.D. Cal. on 2019-07-02 (S15; the PDF text is image-based, quote read from the page image). No evidence of a successor/buyer or any production after 2019 -> project_state paused per D-018 (could equally be 'cancelled'; lead may choose). Status left null: no fetched source documents commercial production (v1 'operational' came from a supplier directory that I could not open; web-search snippet said Komachine lists it as closed 2019 - not usable). Status unconfirmed. All v1 attributes (NMC/pouch/mixed) unverified -> null.

Kawasaki City 2012 document (S19): Phase 1 April Heisei 22 (=2010) 200,000 cells/yr; Phase 2 June Heisei 24 (=2012) 1,000,000 cells/yr. start_year 2010 = Heisei 22 converted; the PDF is image-rendered so the quote cannot be string-matched reliably. Capacity is in cells (cell Wh not published) -> nameplate null; order of magnitude sub-1 GWh. LFP: city document describes iron-phosphate (リン酸鉄) cell; prismatic from product photo in same document - not separately quoted. v1 conflict-free. Coordinates unchanged.

Company site (factory: 223 Chungjusandan 7-ro, Chungju) states it produces lithium-ion cells (Power/Energy/LFP/LTO cell categories) - supports operation but gives no format or capacity. v1 nameplate 1 GWh/yr (ETNews 2024-11-13) could not be verified: english.etnews.com is not reachable from this session and the Rosatom/energy-storage.news article returned 403 -> nameplate null rather than carry unconfirmed. Other figures found only for the planned Russian plant (2 GWh initial / 10 GWh by 2030), a different site. v1 start_year 2001 = company founding, not plant start -> null. v1 pouch/NMC not re-verified -> null.

The Nong Yai (Chonburi) site with Rojana was abandoned: EVLOMO's 2021-09-23 release says it 'has exited MoU with Rojana Industrial Park' (S21) and moved the 8 GWh project to plots in CPGC Industrial Estate, Rayong (S22; construction projected Q1 2022, operations H2 2024). No news after 2021 found that the Rayong plant started; it is not added as a row (stale 2021 plan, no follow-up). Row therefore describes the dead Nong Yai site: project_state cancelled, nameplate nulled (the 8 GWh plan moved to the Rayong site; JV with Rojana ended). v1 coordinates are the Nong Yai point and are unchanged. If the lead prefers one row per project, an alternative is to repoint this row to Rayong and mark project_state paused.

FDK's own Washizu Plant page (614 Washizu, Kosai) lists the plant's product as 'Alkaline batteries' (primary cells) with ISO certifications; the page does not say 'operating' explicitly but is a live corporate site listing. Primary alkaline cells measured in units, no GWh figure -> nameplate null. chemistry 'other' (alkaline primary, not Li-ion). Scope note: primary (non-rechargeable) cell plant - lead may decide whether it belongs in the DB; I did not remove it (it does manufacture cells). v1 cylindrical/consumer not re-verified -> null.

NanoMalaysia subsidiary, 15,000 sq ft plant in Suria Industrial Park, Sepang. Capacity ~1 MWh/yr (= 0.001 GWh/yr, ~92,000 cells) at full scale - a pilot-scale line. Status operational is based on a July 2026 'small-scale production will begin in July' statement (S24, forward-looking; a web-search snippet of an Oct 2026 Business Today item said GMSB is producing and ISO-9001 certified, but the page returned 403 so it is not used) -> confidence 0.4; Aug 2026 Paultan also did not confirm a formal launch. ref_year 2026 = source's full-scale statement (no later phase). v1 start/announced year 2026 not quotable -> null. end_market mixed: just-auto 2026-07-14 says ESS as well as EV batteries (not quoted). v1 coordinates (3.35,101.25) do not look like Sepang (~2.7N,101.7E) - flag for geo audit.

Sella 2 (Eumseong Innovation City) is a 2 GWh/yr cell fab; test cell production began May 2022 (S30), 2 GWh/yr capacity per pv magazine (S29; ref_year 2022 = fallback publication year, no stated full-ramp year). On 2024-12-04 PV Tech reports the SolarEdge Energy Storage Division is closed ('total exit from battery cell and pack manufacturing', S31) and 'the Sella 2 factory in South Korea shuttered ahead of the sale of assets' (S28) -> project_state paused per D-018 (idle, sale pending); no buyer or later news found, so installed null. Status 'operational' = furthest stage reached (test/ramp production 2022-24); commercial mass-production start not quoted -> start_year null. NMC/pouch not confirmed in fetched pages -> null. Note: energy-storage.news pages returned 403 so were not used.

Status unconfirmed. Only v1 source was a supplier directory (not re-openable); no fetched page documents Kokam's Siheung site operating or its capacity. Context: SolarEdge closed the Kokam-based storage division and made a 'total exit from battery cell and pack manufacturing' in Dec 2024 (S31 pv-tech) with ~500 job cuts mostly in Korea, but no source says what happened to Siheung (legacy HQ/cell site) - not removed (no positive evidence it is closed or non-existent). project_state not set. Coordinates unchanged.

Plan: 3.7 GWh/yr of 2170(21700) cells + 12.6 GWh/yr of 4695 cells = 16.3 GWh/yr (Korea Herald 2024-11-06, S32; v1 had the same). ref_year 2024 = fallback (publication year of the plan statement; no stated 达产 year; Kumyang's own 2024 target was mass production 4695 from mid-2025). Latest news (2026-05 to 2026-09): KRX decided to delist Kumyang on 2026-05-20 after two audit disclaimers (injunction pending in Sept); in its February shareholder letter the company said it would accept any investment method 'if only the Gijang plant can be completed' (S34 -> plant NOT complete); a court started auction proceedings over unpaid construction fees on the plant in March 2026 (S35); in Sept 2026 the board decided to spin the Gijang site/buildings/power infrastructure into a data-centre unit KYDC (split date 5 Dec; S56) while saying it is not abandoning batteries. -> status under_construction, project_state paused (stalled and being repurposed; not formally cancelled). No Kumyang evidence that any line is producing. v1 ramp JSON {2026:3.7, 2027:16.3} unsourced -> null. v1 chemistry NCM/EV not re-verified -> null. ESCALATE candidate (16.3 GWh, confidence < 0.6): best-supported value is under_construction + paused.

Output measured in cells, wearable/aviation micro-cells - sub-0.001 GWh; no GWh figure -> nameplate null. The plant was completed Aug 2023 per v1 (etnews, not re-fetched) -> start_year null (no quote). Coordinates unchanged (v1 HQ address may differ from the Dungok plant).

Kusatsu plant (Shiga) began shipping June 2009 with capacity ~110 MWh/yr (MONOist 2011-12-14, S37; company announcement of 2011-12-13). Current (2024-26) status and capacity of Kusatsu not found (i-MiEV production ended ~2021) -> confidence capped 0.35; project_state not evidenced beyond 2011. v1 chemistry/format/end_market not re-verified -> null; jv_partners left as v1 (GS Yuasa, Mitsubishi Corp., Mitsubishi Motors).

Maxell announced (2024-09-13) a ~JPY 5bn investment at the Ono Business Office (Hyogo) to roughly double production capacity by FY2027; the products there are PRIMARY batteries (alkaline button, silver oxide, coin-type lithium) - the page body was partly garbled, quote taken from the fetched page text; auditor please re-check. No GWh figures (coin cells). Scope note: primary-cell plant, like FDK Washizu.

Murata's all-solid-state (oxide, SMD chip) battery line is at the Yasu Plant, 2288 Oshinohara, Yasu City, SHIGA (S40, 2019 release); Nikkan Kogyo 2021-06 says it would mass-produce 100,000 units/month there from 2021 (S39) - this is a plan statement; I found no article confirming the actual start (searches only returned 2019-21 plans), so confidence 0.4 and start_year null. Capacity in micro-cells (mAh class) - negligible GWh -> nameplate null. v1 coordinates (38.1186, 140.7243) are in Miyagi, not Yasu, Shiga (~35.07N, 136.0E) -> set to null (wrong location); lead's geocoder should redo. v1 cell_format 'SMD chip' not in vocabulary -> null.

G-Cell plant, Map Ta Phut, Rayong: started 19 Jul 2021 with 30 MWh/yr, expandable to 100 MWh/yr (GPSC, S41/S42). Business transfer to 24M Technologies closed 30 Aug 2024 (Tilleke & Gibbins, S45, 'from Nuovo Plus'); 24M describes the 6,600 m2 site as a pilot manufacturing facility 'capable of producing up to 100 MWh' and says pilot production has started for an India-based OEM (electrive 2024-09-07, S43/S44). So current owner/operator = 24M (v1 operator Nuovo Plus; id kept per convention) and the JV (Arun Plus/GPSC) no longer applies -> jv_partners null. nameplate 0.1 GWh/yr (capability, ref_year 2024 = 24M publication; 2021 GPSC says expandable to 100 MWh). installed not stated for 2024 -> null (original 30 MWh was 2021, stale). Chemistry: v1 LFP cathode with 24M SemiSolid process; vocabulary value semi-solid-state used. Conflict: Thai PTT-side filings reportedly describe the plant as 30 MWh/yr vs 100 MWh from 24M (search snippet only). Pilot scale, not a gigafactory.

Sekisui Chemical's film product from its pilot line and the planned 100 MW Sakai line is a perovskite SOLAR cell (PV), not an electrochemical battery: pv magazine 2024-12-27 describes 'lightweight, flexible perovskite solar cell products' (Sekisui Solar Film, 100 MW, Sakai, from 2027). The v1 'film battery' label comes from the Japanese 太陽電池 (solar cell). The article does not name Ritto; the Ritto pilot-line attribution is from v1 notes only. v1 already had is_cell_manufacturer false.

Press quote of 300-600 MW/yr (Philstar) is higher than 300 MWh. v1 start_year 2024 not quotable -> null; v1 cell vs pack format not stated -> null. jv_partners left as v1 (StB Capital Partners, Oli Power) - not re-verified.
